activities.caption: file the criteria by their verdict
activities.name: abnDbBuckets

config.prompt: File each candidate criterion of 'abnormal' by its verdict:

items.label: statistical deviance — genius and exceptional calm are rare too
cultural deviance — hearing voices can be a mark of spiritual standing somewhere
homosexuality removed from the manual in 1973
the Rosenhan study's warning about categorical labelling

config.why: Danger is a further but rarely sufficient sign; the criterion of dysfunction did the correcting in 1973 — evidence that same-sex orientation causes no intrinsic dysfunction forced the removal.

activities.caption: pair the manuals and the trade-offs
activities.name: abnDsmMatch

config.prompt: The diagnostic machine — pair each part with its description:

pairs.right: the American manual — descriptive criteria, deliberately agnostic about cause
the WHO manual, used for billing and epidemiology worldwide
two clinicians applying the checklist largely agree — kappa values mostly fair to good
categories may not carve nature at its joints
symptoms and risk genes overlap heavily across diagnoses — the rule, not the exception

config.why: The clinic still needs categories to communicate and plan; the science increasingly thinks in dimensions (HiTOP, RDoC). Both are true, and the tension is productive.

activities.caption: true or false — the three symptom classes
activities.name: abnSchizJudge

statements.s: Positive symptoms are added experiences: hallucinations, delusions, disordered speech.
statements.why: Negative symptoms are the subtracted capacities: avolition, flat affect, social withdrawal, poverty of speech.

statements.s: D2-blocking antipsychotics calm the negative symptoms as effectively as the positive ones.
statements.why: Negative symptoms respond poorly; the dopamine hypothesis accounts best for the positive ones.

statements.s: Working-memory and attention deficits best predict functional outcome.
statements.why: Which is why the cognitive class matters clinically, not just the dramatic symptoms.

statements.s: Tienari's Finnish adoption study found the disorder mainly in high-conflict adoptive homes.
statements.why: The diathesis-stress integration: genes set the dial; environment helps decide where it lands.

config.prompt: The monoamine hypothesis, from pharmacology — order the chain:
items: Reserpine, which depletes serotonin and noradrenaline, induces depression
The first antidepressants increase those monoamines — the hypothesis is born
The clinical response still takes weeks — the full story runs through slower neuroplasticity changes
config.why: Cognitive and learned-helplessness accounts stack alongside: Beck's negative triad dismantled by behavioural experiments, Seligman's uncontrollable stress teaching passivity.

activities.anchor: Setting the expectation correctly is itself clinical work
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a patient-advice leaflet
activities.name: abnAspirinSpot

config.prompt: One line of this patient-advice leaflet is wrong — click it:
lines: Take the medication as prescribed, at the same time each day.
The pharmacological change — more synaptic serotonin — happens within hours.
Expect to feel better by the same evening, the way aspirin works.
Patients who know about the weeks-long delay are less likely to abandon an effective treatment early.
config.correction: The clinical response takes weeks — the full story runs through slower neuroplasticity changes, not a simple chemical top-up.
config.why: Which is one clue that the mechanism is not aspirin-like — and why setting the expectation correctly is itself clinical work.

activities.anchor: The treatment story is the cleanest in the field
activities.caption: fill the extinction mechanism
activities.name: abnExtincCloze

config.text: Exposure works because it enables %%0%% — a new %%1%% memory that the cue no longer predicts harm; avoidance is the maintaining mechanism, and exposure dismantles it.
config.hint: One blank names the learning process; the other names what kind of memory it builds.

activities.caption: order the trap, step by step
activities.name: abnLoopOrder

config.prompt: OCD's escape hatch — order the loop:
items: An intrusive, unwanted thought arrives — contamination, harm to loved ones, forbidden thoughts
A ritual — washing, checking, counting, ordering — neutralises it within seconds
The escape prevents the person from ever learning the obsession is harmless
config.why: The compulsion works — that is the trap. Imaging implicates an orbitofrontal cortex–striatum–thalamus circuit, insight is usually preserved, and response in roughly half to two-thirds of ERP completers shows the exit can be blocked.

activities.anchor: Psychotherapy works: across hundreds of controlled trials
activities.caption: call the meta-analytic verdict
activities.name: abnTherapyEstimate

config.prompt: Across hundreds of controlled trials, the average treated psychotherapy patient ends up better off than about what share of untreated controls?
config.why: About 75–80% — Smith & Glass's classic meta-analysis (effect size around 0.8), repeatedly updated. Not a licence for anything-goes: specific techniques win for specific disorders, and combination treatment beats either alone where trials have run the race.
